correctness.rationale: The complete-square identity reduces Fréchet minimization over curves and independent phase shifts to maximizing the L² norm of their shifted weighted sum. Orthogonality of Fourier modes e^{it} and e^{−it} bounds the squared norm by p²+q², with equality exactly when every same-orientation phase aligns. A common shift removes one phase and leaves the invariant product AB, establishing an exhaustive inequivalent circle of means. mφ becomes a rotated ellipse with semiaxes 1 and |p−q|; at p=q=1/2 it stops twice and retraces the diameter, impossible for a nonconstant periodic trajectory of a locally Lipschitz autonomous planar ODE by uniqueness. For u=e^{it}, b=e^{−it}+εe^{i(t+θ)}, the correlation ε cos(s+θ) has a unique maximizing phase for ε>0 and midpoint curve. Independent exact rational evaluations for ε=1/10,1/4,2/3,9/10 confirm data quotient distance squared 4ε² and unique-mean separation squared 1; the analytic Fourier correlation proves all 0<ε<1.
